title: How should the workbench shelf show that its first row controls the Mark III's pace?
question:
The first item on the training workbench's shelf changes how hard a Mark III's learning pushes each night. Its one, two and three chevrons can stay: they are a universal three-step control. The row still needs a permanent picture that says both robot and pace after purchase, when the sale picture disappears.

I recommend showing the Mark III leaning forward with two short motion trails behind it. That picture stays beside the chevrons after purchase, so the row keeps its meaning in every state. If motion does not read in the shelf's 120-by-72-pixel picture, use a snail, the Mark III and a hare as the three buttons instead. The purchase still applies to one robot, costs 150 gold, and allows the robot to use the bold pace setting when it has assigned squares.
why_now: The pace setting is built with a placeholder picture. The permanent picture should be settled before the shelf art is finished.

options.label: Show a moving Mark III beside the chevrons (Recommended)
options.detail: Draw the Mark III leaning forward with two short motion trails. Keep that picture visible beside the one-, two- and three-chevron buttons before and after purchase. The same picture identifies the robot and pace without adding another animal metaphor.

options.label: Use a snail, the Mark III and a hare as the three buttons
options.detail: Replace the chevrons with custom pictures for calm, normal and bold. The animals make the two ends explicit, but introduce pictures unrelated to the robot and make the middle step depend on their order.

links.caption: The workbench's new sixth plate: the shelf, with the pace setting for sale.
After buying: calm, normal (lit) and bold, as one, two and three chevrons.
The same robot set to bold.

subject: The Mark III learning shop

replies.text: The chevrons stay in the recommended direction. I revised the card around the missing cue: a permanent picture shows the Mark III leaning into motion with two short trails, and it stays beside the chevrons after purchase. This makes the row say robot and pace in every state. A snail, the Mark III and a hare are now the alternative if the moving robot does not read at the shelf's displayed size. The per-robot purchase, 150-gold price and bold setting remain unchanged.
